newsitem.title: SWEDEN: New Celsius head sees most growth in civilian ops.
newsitem.headline: New Celsius head sees most growth in civilian ops.

text.p: Swedish defence and technology group Celsius will grow most through its civilian operations, the company's incoming managing director, Lars Josefsson, said on Thursday.
"The coming year the civil operations will grow quicker than the military one," Josefsson told Reuters.
"I think above all that our work in flying maintenance seems positive."

Josefsson, who is to take over from Olle Lund on June 1 when Lund retires after 13 years of heading the company, said he saw a lot of synergies between the military and the civilian parts of the company.

"Our investment in high technology gives synergies in all areas. A good example is in the Information Technology area with the expansion in simulated systems," he said after his appointment was announced on Thursday.
Civil engineer Josefsson, currently managing director at Ericsson Austria AG, said structural changes in Europe's defence industry would affect Celsius over the next five years.
"In a five-year point of view, Celsius will have participated in structural changes on the defence side," he said.
He said large costs savings would come from these changes.
"But it is really theoretical, and I can not clearly know how or when such structural changes will come about," he said.
Josefsson said Celsius must also improve its profitability and give shareholders better returns.
"For Celsius to have satisfied shareholders we must increase profitability," Josefsson said.
"'Shareholder Value' is a key word for me."
